newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communist minister against privatisations.
newsitem.headline: French Communist minister against privatisations.

text.p: France's newly appointed Transport Minister Jean-Claude Gayssot said he was not going to be the minister of the privatisation of Air France and rail group SNCF but he would also not completely overhaul the restructuring programmes started at these companies.
In an interview with France Inter radio, Gayssot said he wanted to consult and discuss with the people invloved before making decisions.
"We have to restructure, but make positive restructurings," Gayssot said.
"Nobody expects that Gayssot will become the minister or privatisations, deregulation and ultra-liberalism... I believe there is a role for the public service," he said.
As a deputy, Gayssot was opposed to the financial restructuring of SNCF, splitting the infrastructure and operating activities.
But he said on Thursday that the restructuring had now been voted by parliament. "I am going to consult on and study this issue in further detail and I will move forward in consultation."

On Air France, which the previous government planned to privatise at the end of this year, Gayssot said "People say that the need to modernise and adapt...is opposed to the public service. That is not my opinion."

"I believe that in a country, in Europe, there is a need for public services.. and this not in a framework of withdrawal to a few activities but on the contrary a development in the interests of the employees, the users and security," he said.
